tool: ggml_ops_capture.py, ggml_ops_score.py (with ggml_ops.py over ggml_shim/), exl3_heldout.py --variant ggml_ops, oracle_compare.py, tierc.py
interpretation: Reference-only measurements for choosing the GGML paths native EXL3 uses for its non-linear operations. Operation level: every captured operation of frozen EXL3-G (layers 0, 6, 12, 18, 23; each prefix's prefill and single-token steps 0 and 15; both fixtures) recomputed in FP64 from its captured inputs; upstream's captured output and each GGML candidate's output on the same inputs compared with it. Full model: the recommended plan as a Tier C arm (ggml_ops), scored against the FP64 oracle with the third pass's arms. No timing was measured.

pins.profile: EXL3-G: EXL3_GEMV=0, EXL3_HGEMM_F16ACC=0, frozen tune-40-gemvoff / tune-45-gemvoff (copies), EXL3_BC_ATTN=0 (bit-identical)

path_study.shapes: Qwen2.5-0.5B: 14 query heads, 2 KV heads (GQA ratio 7), head dim 64, F16 K/V cache, causal; prefill 32/144/145/1023/1024 rows; single-token steps attending to 33..1040 positions
path_study.build_flags: ggml-cuda compiles with -use_fast_math (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/CMakeLists.txt:186): sinf/cosf/expf/powf/division become approximate intrinsics in every GGML kernel below; ExLlamaV3's extension also compiles with --use_fast_math (exllamav3/ext.py:92)

ggml_flash_attn_ext.selection: ggml_cuda_get_best_fattn_kernel (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/fattn.cu:517-651). GB10 has Turing-class MMA (fattn.cu:614). Vector kernel only if K's length is a multiple of FATTN_KQ_STRIDE=256 (fattn.cu:611, fattn-common.cuh:9) and, for F16 K/V on cc >= Ada, Q has one column (fattn.cu:614-618; the gqa_ratio > 4 exception needs K >= 8192). Otherwise the MMA-F16 kernel (fattn.cu:635). Tile and WMMA are not selected on GB10. llama.cpp pads n_kv to at least 256 (src/llama-kv-cache.cpp:1250-1260), so its decode takes the vector kernel and every prefill of these shapes the MMA kernel. Measured: GGML's automatic choice with K padded is bit-identical to the forced vector launcher on all 100 captured single-token cases; without padding decode takes MMA.
ggml_flash_attn_ext.precision_option: ggml_flash_attn_ext_set_prec is deprecated in favour of ggml_prec_set_acc, which writes op_params[3] (ggml/src/ggml.c:3282-3301, 5542-5549); no CUDA flash-attention file reads op_params[3] (only 0-2 and 4: fattn-common.cuh:1095,1215-1217; fattn.cu:121-122), so the precision request has no effect on CUDA at this pin. llama.cpp sets it anyway (src/llama-graph.cpp:2639).
ggml_flash_attn_ext.vec: flash_attn_ext_vec (fattn-vec.cuh). On NVIDIA V_DOT2_F32_F16_AVAILABLE is undefined (it is HIP-only, ggml/src/ggml-cuda/common.cuh:769-771), so Q stays F32 (scaled), K and V are converted to F32, KQ is accumulated in F32 (fattn-common.cuh:88-115), softmax in F32 and VKQ accumulated in float2 (fattn-vec.cuh:124-130). Scratch: launch_fattn splits the KV sequence over parallel blocks and combines partial results from the pool (fattn-common.cuh:1013-1014, 1129-1200). Scores are never materialized.
ggml_flash_attn_ext.mma_f16: flash_attn_ext_f16 (fattn-mma-f16.cuh): Q converted to F16; KQ by mma.sync m16n8k16 F16 inputs with F32 accumulators (T_C_KQ float, fattn-mma-f16.cuh:1068-1084; mma.cuh:1163); softmax in F32; probabilities converted to F16 and VKQ accumulated in F16 (T_C_VKQ half2, fattn-mma-f16.cuh:1075/1083; mma.sync ...f16.f16.f16.f16, mma.cuh:977). Stream-K fixup scratch from the pool. Scores not materialized.
ggml_flash_attn_ext.tile: flash_attn_ext_tile (fattn-tile.cuh): with FAST_FP16_AVAILABLE (NVIDIA, common.cuh:271-272) Q and K are half2, products formed in F16 and summed in F32 (common.cuh:773-786; Q pre-scaled against overflow, fattn-tile.cuh:628-632), VKQ accumulated in half2 (fattn-tile.cuh:888, 688-693). Reachable on GB10 only by calling its launcher (ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_tile, fattn-tile.cuh:1338).
ggml_flash_attn_ext.wmma: AMD only (fattn.cu:666-669); not built for NVIDIA.

non_flash.graph: llama.cpp's build_attn_mha (src/llama-graph.cpp:2660-2700): kq = mul_mat(K, Q) with ggml_prec_set_acc(GGML_PREC_F32); soft_max_ext(kq, F32 mask, scale); kqv = mul_mat(V^T, P) at default precision; V stored transposed.
non_flash.routing: ggml_cuda_mul_mat (ggml/src/ggml-cuda/ggml-cuda.cu:1823-1877): MMVF, MMF, then cuBLAS. From GGML's own predicates at these shapes (nonfa_routes): single-token KQ and KQV take MMVF up to n_kv 1023 and KQ takes MMF from 1024; every prefill takes cuBLAS for both.
non_flash.cublas_precision: ggml_cuda_mul_mat_cublas (ggml-cuda.cu:1622-1669): GGML_PREC_F32 or GGML_CUDA_CUBLAS_COMPUTE_TYPE=f32 selects F32 compute, converting F16 K to an F32 pool copy (ggml-cuda.cu:1446-1470) and calling cublasGemmBatchedEx with CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F (GQA broadcast, ggml-cuda.cu:1576-1614); the handle GGML creates has CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH (common.cuh:1544), which lets cuBLAS round F32 inputs to TF32. Default precision on F16 V selects CUBLAS_COMPUTE_16F with an F16 copy of the probabilities and an F16 output temporary converted back to F32 (traits, ggml-cuda.cu:1395-1406, 1510-1530, 1616-1619).
non_flash.memory: Materializes the scores: KQ [n_kv_pad, n_q, 14] F32 and the softmax output, plus the V^T copy and the pool copies above.

path_study.rms_norm: ggml_rms_norm is F32-only (norm.cu:484-485); rms_norm_f32 (norm.cu:77-150): F32 sum of squares, block reduction, rsqrtf(mean + eps), dst = scale * x (* mul). ggml_cuda_op_rms_norm_fused (norm.cu:502-527, F32 weight required) is chosen by the graph-compute fusion check; the fused kernel computes (scale*x)*w exactly as rms_norm followed by mul, and was bit-identical to the unfused pair on all 330 captured cases.
path_study.rope: ggml_cuda_op_rope (rope.cu:696); NEOX in F32 or F16 (same kernel template on either type); theta_scale = powf(freq_base, -2/n_dims) (rope.cu:388), theta = pos * powf(theta_scale, i0/2) (rope.cu:107, 182), cos/sin by cosf/sinf (rope.cu:36-37), all approximate under -use_fast_math. F16 in/out computes in F32 and rounds once; on every captured case it equalled F32 compute rounded by GGML's copy (300/300).
path_study.swiglu: ggml_swiglu_split -> ggml_cuda_op_swiglu (unary.cu:348): silu(x) * g with ggml_cuda_op_silu_single = x / (1 + expf(-x)) (unary.cuh:98-100), F32 or F16 data.
path_study.add: ggml_cuda_op_add (binbcast.cu:437): one F32 add per element.
path_study.get_rows: ggml_cuda_op_get_rows (getrows.cu): gathers rows converting F16/BF16 to F32 (exact).
path_study.conversion: ggml_cpy F32 -> F16 rounds to nearest (cpy-utils.cuh).

build.script: ggml_shim/build.sh (CMake project ggml_shim/CMakeLists.txt), inside llmp-exl3-reference:20260922; the SDK's CMake, the container's GCC 13.3.0 (-march=armv8-a) as C, C++ and CUDA host compiler; GGML's own CMake options: BUILD_SHARED_LIBS=ON, GGML_BACKEND_DL=OFF, GGML_NATIVE=OFF, GGML_CUDA=ON, GGML_CUDA_NCCL=OFF, GGML_CUDA_GRAPHS=OFF, GGML_OPENMP=OFF, no tests/examples, Release; CMAKE_CUDA_ARCHITECTURES=121-real, mapped by GGML to 121a-real
build.nvcc_flags_ggml_cuda: -O3 -std=c++17 --generate-code=arch=compute_121a,code=[sm_121a] -Xcompiler=-fPIC -use_fast_math -extended-lambda -compress-mode=size -Xcompiler "-Wmissing-declarations -Wmissing-noreturn -Wall -Wextra -Wpedantic -Wcast-qual -Wno-unused-function -Wno-array-bounds -Wextra-semi -Wno-pedantic" (-ccbin cxx-target = g++ -march=armv8-a); definitions GGML_CUDA_FA_QUANTS=q4_0-q4_0,q8_0-q8_0,f16-f16,bf16-bf16, GGML_SCHED_MAX_COPIES=4, GGML_SHARED, GGML_BACKEND_BUILD, GGML_BACKEND_SHARED

cuda130.nvcc: 13.0.88 (the host's /usr/local/cuda-13.0, as the reference's extension build)

cuda134.nvcc: 13.4.92 (the SDK's CUDA 13.4 tree with 13.0 headers overlaid, p0-20260925/cuda-bridge-torch mounted at /cuda, as exl3_run.sh's bridge mode)

identity_13_0_vs_13_4.note: every GGML candidate output of the operation study (ggml_ops_score.py --hashes, then --compare-hashes)

build.difference_from_bridge: The FP16 bridge builds llama.cpp with the SDK's Clang host compiler and NVCC 13.4, static libraries, for sm_121a. This harness uses the container's GCC 13.3 host compiler and shared libraries so it loads next to PyTorch; built with NVCC 13.0 (the container's toolkit) and with NVCC 13.4, the two give identical outputs on every case. At run time both use PyTorch's CUDA runtime 13.0 (cudaRuntimeGetVersion 13000) and PyTorch's cuBLAS; the recommended plan makes no cuBLAS call.
build.shim: ggml_shim.cu: C API; inputs copied device-to-device into tensors of a GGML CUDA buffer (ggml_gallocr); one-operation graphs through ggml_backend_graph_compute, or the vector/tile flash-attention launcher called directly with the backend's context; a counting ggml_cuda_pool replaces GGML's VMM pool to measure operation scratch. The ggml_cuda_init device-flag side effect (cudaSetDeviceFlags(cudaDeviceScheduleSpin) on cc 12.1, ggml-cuda.cu:366-369) runs in these processes; it affects synchronization only.

notes: Statistics per case: max_abs, rms, rel_rms = RMS error / RMS of the FP64 result; aggregated per phase over the captured layers (rel_rms_max, rel_rms_mean, max of max_abs, RMS of rms); attention adds each query row's relative RMS error (row_rel_rms_max, quantiles).

Candidates ending _f16 are the F32 result rounded to F16 by GGML's copy (what an F16 linear input or the F16 cache receives); for attention the F16 rounding was done in PyTorch after checking, on the 32-row prefills, that GGML's copy gives the same bits (80/80).
rope_attention: q from each RoPE candidate applied to the captured pre-RoPE q, then attention over the captured cache, against FP64 RoPE then FP64 attention; upstream is its captured output.

scratch_bytes: GGML pool peak (counting pool) and materialized graph intermediates per call; for upstream attention, PyTorch's allocation peak above the call's start less its output. The GGML figures for rms_norm/rope/swiglu include the shim's own F32<->F16 conversion tensors.
Single-token SiLU gating runs inside upstream's graphed C++ MLP and was not captured; prefill captures cover the operation.

plan.embedding: GGML get_rows on the BF16 table to F32: bit-identical to upstream's lookup (10/10).
plan.rms_norm: GGML rms_norm + mul in F32 on the FP32 residual stream (fused or unfused; identical, 330/330), output converted to F16 by GGML's copy for the linear inputs (final norm likewise). Accuracy equal to upstream's: relative-RMS ratio 1.00 in every phase; bit-identical to upstream in 211 of 330 cases, the rest differ by one F16 rounding with equal error statistics.
plan.residual_add: GGML add in F32: bit-identical to upstream's fused residual add (150/150).
plan.rope: GGML NEOX RoPE computed in F32 on the F16 projections; q kept F32 for attention, k rounded to F16 for the cache (bit-identical to computing in F16). The F16-output path has upstream's accuracy (ratio 1.00); keeping q in F32 removes that rounding (6.2e-7 to 3.8e-5 relative RMS, 0.003-0.16x upstream).
plan.attention: ggml_flash_attn_ext with F16 K/V, F32 q, through the vector kernel for every phase: in decode that is GGML's own choice once K is padded to 256 (bit-identical, 100/100); for prefill the launcher is called directly (ggml_cuda_flash_attn_ext_vec_case<64, F16, F16>), a recorded plan choice. Output converted to F16 by GGML's copy for o_proj. F32 relative RMS 2.3e-6 to 4.1e-6 against upstream's 2.2e-4 to 3.6e-4 (0.009-0.017x); after the F16 rounding 0.82-0.99x upstream; with q from F32 RoPE, 0.24-0.49x upstream (rope_attention).
plan.swiglu: GGML swiglu on the FP32 gate and up, output converted to F16: bit-identical to upstream (50/50). Single-token steps take the same path once the graphed MLP is off (logits unchanged, capture manifests).

memory.attention_vec: Scores never materialized. Pool scratch (partial results of the split KV loop): 354,816 B at a 32-row prefill, 1,596,672 / 1,607,760 B at 144 / 145 rows, 11,343,024 / 11,356,160 B at 1,023 / 1,024 rows (about n_q x 14 x (64 + 2) x 4 B x 3 parallel blocks); 14,784 B per single-token step up to 160 positions, 48,048 B at 1,023-1,039.
memory.upstream_attention: Triton prefill: no allocation beyond its output (0 B; 256 B at 145 rows); Triton flash-decoding: 279,296 B per single-token step.
memory.alternatives: MMA (fa_auto prefill): 557,056 B at 32 rows, 1,671,168-1,671,680 B from 144 rows. Non-flash: 1,097,728 B of intermediates at 32 rows, 4.7 MB at 144-145, 121,372,672 B at 1,024 rows (the F32 scores and probabilities), plus pool copies (llama.cpp precision: up to 31,195,472 B at 1,024 rows).
memory.against_upstream_phase_peaks: The vector kernel's decode scratch is below upstream's (48 KB vs 279 KB). Its prefill scratch exceeds upstream's attention scratch (none) at every prefill, and exceeds upstream's whole non-logit phase peak (README, per-phase memory: 229,888 B at 32 rows, 1,032,704 B at 144 rows) by 124,928 B and 563,968 B; from 145 rows it is smaller than that peak (2.7% of it at 145 rows, 17-18% at 1,023-1,024); whether it raises the peak depends on what is live at the time, which was not measured. No GGML attention path stays within upstream's prefill scratch: MMA needs 557 KB-1.67 MB, non-flash 1.1-121 MB. If the per-phase limit is strict at 32 and 144 rows, those prefills need the owner's call (for instance a vector launcher with one parallel block, a recorded K-L departure, not measured here).

recommendation.why: Every GGML operation except attention is equal to upstream (bit-identical or the same F16 rounding). For attention the most accurate GGML path is the vector kernel, F32 throughout on NVIDIA; the MMA kernel GGML picks for prefill accumulates V*P in F16 and is up to 2.8x less accurate than upstream at 1,023-1,024 rows (row maximum 1.4e-3 to 1.8e-3 against 3.3e-4 to 3.5e-4); tile is 13-24x less accurate; llama.cpp's non-flash graph (F16 KQV compute) up to 2.8x; non-flash with both products at GGML_PREC_F32 comes close to vec (2.3e-6 to 7.2e-6) only with TF32 disabled on the handle (with GGML's TF32 handle, 1.3e-4 to 1.8e-4 at prefill), and materializes 121 MB of scores at 1,024 rows.

tier_c_arms.superseded_by: tierc.json (the committed Tier C bounds and calibration, with the ggml_ops and ggml_ops_cublas138b arms among its 15 legitimate arms; scores score-v5-*). This section is the earlier, intermediate scoring (score-v4-*), kept as recorded; its bounds and ratios are not the ones in force.
tier_c_arms.variant: exl3_heldout.py --variant ggml_ops (VARIANTS and apply_variant only), library /p0/ggmlops/cuda130/libggml_shim.so via GGML_OPS_LIB; harness SHA-256 eec6e25180bb243fe228f1284d321be617536ab44d2b967806d1b5dfee98a25c
tier_c_arms.runs: v3-40-ggml_ops, v3-45-ggml_ops (PyTorch's cuBLAS 13.1.1, cuBLASLt 130101) and v3-40/45-ggml_ops_cublas138b (the SDK's 13.8.0.4 bind-mounted as v3-*-cublas138b, cuBLASLt 130800 the only one mapped); --gemv off --hgemm-f16acc 0 --capture; each passed every repeat, restore and capture check; frozen caches unchanged
tier_c_arms.scores: oracle_compare.py over the 18 third-pass arms plus these two, per fixture (p0-20260925/oracle/score-v4-40.json, score-v4-45.json); tierc.py (the repository's current version, distinct-value medians) --thresholds 2 8
tier_c_arms.summary: The ggml_ops arms sit inside the legitimate spread: leave-one-out maxima 1.09 / 1.75 (4.0 bpw) and 1.07 / 1.49 (4.5 bpw), with cuBLAS 13.8 1.15 / 1.79 and 1.07 / 1.34 (averaged / extreme; thresholds 2 / 8). Against the committed tierc.json bounds they reach at most 0.58 of the averaged and 0.23 of the extreme bound. Geometric mean of their statistics over the frozen arm's: 0.99-1.01. The two subtle faults still pass and the four gross faults still fail with these arms included (check.separates is false only because of the subtle faults, as in the third pass).

TUNE=<copy of tune-40-gemvoff.bin> sh harness/ggml_ops_run.sh ggml_ops_capture.py --model /experiment/models/4.0bpw --ids /p0/heldout-ids.i64le --pins /p0/exl3/pins.json --reference /p0/exl3/v3-40-g --output /p0/ggmlops/cap-40 --check-mlp-bc (and 4.5bpw).

This file's operation_accuracy is the cuda130 output.

Arms: per fixture (NN = 40 or 45), with a fresh copy of the frozen tune-NN-gemvoff.bin as the arm's cache: DOCKER_EXTRA="-e GGML_OPS_LIB=/p0/ggmlops/cuda130/libggml_shim.so" exl3_run.sh v3-NN-ggml_ops FIXTURE tune-v3-NN-ggml_ops.bin --gemv off --hgemm-f16acc 0 --capture --variant ggml_ops, and the same as v3-NN-ggml_ops_cublas138b with DOCKER_EXTRA adding the two read-only bind mounts of the SDK's libcublas.so.13 and libcublasLt.so.13 (13.8.0.4) over PyTorch's in nvidia/cu13/lib (README, second pass); then oracle_compare.py ORACLE over each fixture's v3-NN-* runs and tierc.py SCORES --thresholds 2 8 (README, reproduction: third pass).
